h1: The 7 Best Samsung Soundbars for Every Room and Budget in 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 Samsung soundbars from the B-Series to the Q-Series flagship, compared on channel count, Atmos, Q-Symphony and value.
summary: The Samsung HW-Q900H is the soundbar to buy if you want the newest flagship, with 7.1.2 channels and an included subwoofer. The Q800F is the better value at 5.1.2 channels with Game Mode Pro, the refurbished Q990D delivers 11.1.4 channels with a protection bundle, and the B-Series B400F is the cheapest way to get a built-in subwoofer.
intro: Samsung's naming trips up more buyers than any other soundbar maker. A bar called 5.1.2 does not simply sound three times better than a 2.1, and the channel count on the box says little about what will happen in a living room with an open floor plan. What changes your evenings is whether the bar can bounce sound off the ceiling, whether it pairs with your Samsung TV's own speakers, and whether the subwoofer is a separate box or built in.

We reviewed seven Samsung soundbars across the B-Series, S-Series and Q-Series, including a refurbished flagship and a 2021 model that is still sold. The ranking leans on named features in each listing, including Dolby Atmos, Q-Symphony and Game Mode Pro, and we are careful to flag where a listing leaves out the power rating or connection details.

products.name: Samsung Q-Series Soundbar (HW-Q900H, 2026 Model), 7.1.2ch + Subwoofer
products.verdict: Samsung's newest flagship, with 7.1.2 channels and a subwoofer in the box.
products.description:
The HW-Q900H is a 2026 Q-Series soundbar with a 7.1.2 channel layout and an included subwoofer. In that notation the first number counts the front and surround channels, the second the subwoofer and the last the upward-firing height channels, which is how Dolby Atmos reaches overhead.

It takes the top spot because it brings Samsung's current flagship design to a price below the 11.1.4 models. Seven channels plus two height speakers is enough for convincing overhead effects in a normal room, and it is the newest silicon in the ranking, so software support should last longest. It costs $500 and up, which is the major tradeoff, and it is not the cheapest route to Atmos.

Buy it if you want one flagship bar for a main room and plan to keep it for years. Make sure your TV has an eARC port.
cons: Needs a capable TV for full features
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a long-lived flagship for the main room.

products.name: Samsung Q800F 5.1.2ch Q Series Soundbar + Subwoofer, Wireless Dolby Atmos, Q-Symphony, Game Mode Pro (2025)
products.verdict: A current Q-Series bar with Atmos, Q-Symphony and Game Mode Pro for less than the flagship.
products.description:
The Q800F is a 2025 Q-Series soundbar with a 5.1.2 channel layout, an included subwoofer, wireless Dolby Atmos, Q-Symphony and Game Mode Pro. Q-Symphony lets the bar and a compatible Samsung TV share the work of playing sound, while Game Mode Pro tunes the audio for gaming.

It ranks second because it hits the sweet spot between feature set and price. Five channels and two height speakers give a real sense of overhead sound, and the subwoofer ships in the box. What you give up against the Q900H is two channels and the newest model year. It costs $500 and up, so it sits in the same price tier.

Buy it if you game or watch movies on a Samsung TV and want the key Q-Series features. Skip it if you have a non-Samsung TV and want a deeper bar.
pros: Game Mode Pro for console gaming
products.idealFor: Samsung TV owners who game and watch films.

products.name: Samsung (Refurbished) HW-Q990D Q-Series 11.1.4ch Wireless Dolby Soundbar with Q-Symphony (2024)
products.verdict: The 2024 flagship with 11.1.4 channels, sold refurbished with a 2-year protection bundle.
products.description:
The HW-Q990D is Samsung's 2024 flagship soundbar, with an 11.1.4 channel layout, wireless Dolby sound and Q-Symphony. This listing is a refurbished unit sold with a 2-year protection bundle, and it costs $500 and up.

It ranks third because the channel count is the highest in the ranking, with four height channels and the widest surround spread. The refurbished status and a protection bundle make it a reasonable gamble, but a refurbished unit is still a risk compared with a new one. It sits below the Q900H and Q800F because they are newer and arrive as new retail products.

Buy it if you want maximum channel count and accept refurbished stock. Check the return terms and the protection bundle details before ordering.
pros: Highest channel count in the ranking
products.idealFor: Home theater fans who want a large surround bar and accept refurbished.
products.skipIf: You only buy new products with a full warranty.

products.name: SAMSUNG S60D 5.0ch Soundbar with Wireless Dolby Atmos, Q-Symphony, Alexa Built-in
products.verdict: A 5.0 channel bar with Atmos, Q-Symphony and Alexa for $200 to $500.
products.description:
The S60D is a 5.0 channel soundbar with wireless Dolby Atmos, Q-Symphony and Alexa built in, priced from $200 to $500. The .0 in the layout means no separate subwoofer comes in the box.

It ranks fourth because it offers the mid-tier features Samsung TV owners want without the cost of the Q-Series. Atmos and Q-Symphony are included, and Alexa lets you control it by voice. The missing subwoofer is the real compromise, because bass is thin from a bar this size. You can add one later if Samsung's pairing allows.

Buy it for a bedroom or small living room with a Samsung TV. Skip it if low bass is a priority.
pros: Atmos and Q-Symphony at mid price
Alexa built in for voice control
Five channels for a wide stage
products.idealFor: Small to mid-size rooms with a Samsung TV.
products.skipIf: You want deep bass out of the box.

products.name: Samsung B-Series Soundbar HW-B550F 2.1ch DTS Virtual:X with Subwoofer (2025 Model)
products.verdict: A 2.1 channel bar with DTS Virtual:X, a subwoofer and adaptive sound.
products.description:
The HW-B550F is a 2025 B-Series 2.1 channel soundbar with an included subwoofer, DTS Virtual:X, bass boost and adaptive sound, and it costs $200 to $500. Virtual:X uses processing to simulate a wider and taller sound field.

It ranks fifth because it adds a separate subwoofer and virtual surround to the entry B-Series, but it is a stereo-plus-sub bar underneath, with no true height or rear channels. Compared with the S60D it gives up real Atmos but adds bass. It also trails the cheaper B400F only because that model undercuts it by a large margin.

Buy it if you want bigger sound than a TV and a separate subwoofer on a mid-range budget. Do not expect cinema-style overhead effects.
pros: Bass Boost for extra low end
products.idealFor: Buyers who want clearer dialogue and bass for a moderate outlay.
products.skipIf: You want real Atmos overhead channels.

products.name: SAMSUNG HW-Q950A 11.1.4ch Soundbar with Dolby Atmos/DTS:X, Alexa Built-in (2021), Black
products.verdict: A 2021 11.1.4 flagship with Atmos and DTS:X, now several generations old.
products.description:
The HW-Q950A is a 2021 soundbar with an 11.1.4 channel layout, Dolby Atmos and DTS:X support and Alexa built in. It costs $500 and up and is sold as a legacy model.

It ranks sixth because age is the problem. The channel count still matches the 2024 flagship, but newer bars have more recent connectivity and software, and a 2021 unit's pricing may no longer reflect its age. The upside is DTS:X support, which the newer models do not list in these titles.

Buy it only if the price has dropped well below the newer bars, and verify what is included before ordering. Otherwise a current-generation Q-Series model is the better long-term purchase.
products.idealFor: DTS:X collectors who find it well below the new price.
products.skipIf: You want the newest connectivity and software.

products.name: Samsung B-Series Soundbar HW B400F 2.0ch with Built-In Subwoofer (2025 Model)
products.verdict: The cheapest Samsung bar here, with a built-in subwoofer and Voice Enhance mode.
products.description:
The HW-B400F is a 2.0 channel 2025 B-Series soundbar with a built-in subwoofer and Voice Enhance mode, and it costs $50 to $100. Built in means the bass driver lives inside the bar rather than in a separate box.

It ranks last because 2.0 channels and a built-in sub cannot match the stage or the bass depth of the larger bars. It earns its place by being the cheapest, easiest upgrade over TV speakers, with Voice Enhance mode helping dialogue stand out. There is no surround or Atmos, and the listing names no other connections.

Buy it for a bedroom or a secondary TV where simplicity and cost matter. Skip it if you watch action films or music at volume.
cons: Bass is limited by the small driver
products.idealFor: Bedrooms and secondary TVs with a small budget.
products.skipIf: You want a cinematic or music-focused sound.

methodology.title: Channel layout
methodology.description: We compared channel counts such as 2.0, 5.1.2 and 11.1.4, and checked whether height channels exist for real Dolby Atmos effects.

methodology.title: Subwoofer design
methodology.description: Separate, built-in and missing subwoofers were rated for bass depth, since low frequencies are where soundbars differ most.

methodology.title: Samsung ecosystem features
methodology.description: Q-Symphony, wireless Atmos, Game Mode Pro and Alexa support were weighed for owners of compatible Samsung TVs.

methodology.title: Model age and support
methodology.description: Newer model years and new-condition products outranked legacy and refurbished units, because software and connectivity age quickly.

methodology.title: Value
methodology.description: Price ranges from $50 to $500 and up were weighed against channel count and features to find the best return in each tier.

whatMatters.detail: A rating such as 5.1.2 lists the front and surround channels, then the subwoofer, then the upward-firing height speakers. More channels means more places for sound to come from, but only if your room can reflect it. In small rooms, a 5.1.2 bar often sounds as complete as an 11.1.4 one.

Atmos adds overhead sound by firing speakers at the ceiling or by processing, and it needs height channels to work properly. Look for a number after the second dot, like the 2 in 7.1.2. A flat 2.1 or 5.0 bar can accept Atmos signals but cannot reproduce real height.

Q-Symphony lets a compatible Samsung TV and soundbar play audio together, so your TV speakers act as extra channels. It only works with recent Samsung TVs, so check your model before paying for it. Non-Samsung TVs still send audio through HDMI eARC but lose this feature.

A separate wireless subwoofer can sit anywhere in the room and usually moves more air than a built-in driver. A built-in sub saves space and money but limits bass depth. Check whether the sub is included, since the S60D ships without one.

HDMI eARC is the cleanest way to send Atmos from a TV to the bar, and it uses a single cable. Without it, you may be limited to a lower-quality digital connection. Look at your TV's ports and confirm the bar supports the same HDMI standard before buying.

howToChoose.intro: Channel layout sets the size of the sound stage, so start with how big a sound you want and how big your room is.

cards.label: True Atmos
cards.text: Dedicated upward-firing speakers bounce sound off the ceiling for height effects. The Q900H, Q800F, Q990D, Q950A and S60D lists support Atmos, and the ones with a .2 or .4 have height channels.

cards.label: Virtual surround
cards.text: Processing simulates a wider sound field from forward-facing speakers. The B550F uses DTS Virtual:X, which is pleasant but cannot match real overhead channels.

howToChoose.note: Choose true Atmos for a room with a flat ceiling and a main movie seat, and virtual surround for a small budget.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Height channels for Atmos, a separate subwoofer and a clear dialogue mode. Placement under the TV and a few feet from the back wall matters for the surround spread.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Samsung HW-Q900H and the Q800F are the cleanest cinema picks, and the refurbished Q990D adds the most channels for large rooms.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a large room, a Samsung TV and a love of Atmos films. The Q900H and Q800F repay the $500 and up with height channels and a real subwoofer.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mostly watch the news, shows or streaming dialogue. The B400F at $50 to $100 and the B550F at $200 to $500 improve on TV speakers for far less.

faq.q: Do Samsung soundbars work with non-Samsung TVs?
faq.a: Yes, they connect through HDMI eARC or optical like any soundbar. You lose Samsung-specific features such as Q-Symphony, which needs a compatible Samsung TV. Core sound, Atmos and Alexa features still work.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake buying a Samsung soundbar?
faq.a: Choosing by channel count alone. An 11.1.4 bar in a small room often sounds no better than a 5.1.2. Match the bar to the room, and check that your TV has an eARC port.

faq.q: Is a Q-Series bar worth it over the B-Series?
faq.a: If you care about film, gaming or Atmos, yes. The Q-Series adds height channels, a wireless subwoofer and richer bass. B-Series models are fine for clearer dialogue and a modest upgrade.

faq.q: How do I set up Q-Symphony?
faq.a: Connect the bar to a compatible Samsung TV with HDMI, enable Q-Symphony in the TV's sound settings and select the soundbar as the output. Make sure both devices have the latest firmware. The TV's speakers then work together with the bar.

faq.q: Is a refurbished soundbar a good idea?
faq.a: It can be if it comes with a protection bundle like the one offered with the HW-Q990D. Refurbished stock has been inspected but not freshly built. Check the return terms and the length of coverage first.

faq.q: Can I add a subwoofer to the S60D later?
faq.a: The S60D ships without one, and adding a compatible wireless subwoofer depends on Samsung's pairing support. Check Samsung's compatibility list for the exact model. If bass matters, start with a bar that includes the sub.

finalTake: The Samsung HW-Q900H is the best soundbar here for anyone who wants the newest flagship, while the Q800F delivers nearly the same experience with Game Mode Pro for less. Home theater buyers who are comfortable with a refurbished unit should consider the HW-Q990D, and anyone on a budget should start with the B550F or the B400F. Skip the 2021 HW-Q950A unless the price is clearly lower than the newer bars.
